summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation on warfarin, hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, and prior strokes presented with acute onset nausea, vomiting, posterior headache, and imbalance. MRI confirmed an acute to subacute left cerebellar infarction. He was admitted to the neurology stroke service, briefly monitored in the ICU due to supratherapeutic INR and concern for swelling, but required no surgical intervention. His warfarin was held and later restarted, and aspirin was reduced to 81 mg to minimize bleeding risk. He showed clinical improvement in coordination and gait, was able to ambulate independently, and was discharged home on day four with outpatient physical therapy, medication adjustments including a switch to atorvastatin, and close follow-up for stroke prevention and diabetes management.
